description: IPC mechanisms decomposed across the spectrum: pipes (simple byte streams), Unix domain sockets (rich semantics + fd passing), shared memory + futex (highest throughput), signals (async notification), eventfd + signalfd + timerfd (modern Linux event integration), io_uring (covered in network), memfd_create. The trade-offs in latency, throughput, complexity, and what each is good for.

sub_mechanisms.name: anonymous_pipe
sub_mechanisms.definition: pipe() returns two fds: read end + write end. Bytes written to one come out the other. Kernel buffers ~64 KB.
sub_mechanisms.why: Simplest IPC. Survives fork (child + parent both have fds). Foundation of shell pipelines. Cost: kernel buffer + read/write copies vs shared memory.

sub_mechanisms.name: pipe_blocking_semantics
sub_mechanisms.definition: Writer blocks when buffer full; reader blocks when buffer empty. EOF when all write ends closed.
sub_mechanisms.why: Natural flow control. SIGPIPE on write to a pipe with no readers. O_NONBLOCK flag enables polling instead of blocking. Standard producer-consumer semantics.

sub_mechanisms.name: unix_socket_stream
sub_mechanisms.definition: AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM. Bidirectional, ordered, reliable byte stream between processes on same host.
sub_mechanisms.why: Most-featured local IPC. Connection-oriented (accept + connect). Used by X11, postgresql, docker.sock. Avoids loopback TCP's overhead (no checksums, no fragmentation).

sub_mechanisms.name: unix_socket_dgram
sub_mechanisms.definition: AF_UNIX SOCK_DGRAM. Connectionless, message-oriented, reliable on local host.
sub_mechanisms.why: Message boundaries preserved (vs SOCK_STREAM's byte stream). Used for short request-reply protocols. systemd uses for sd-bus.

sub_mechanisms.name: fd_passing_SCM_RIGHTS
sub_mechanisms.definition: Unix socket can carry file descriptors via SCM_RIGHTS ancillary data. Receiver gets a duplicate of the sender's fd.
sub_mechanisms.why: Lets one process pass open files/sockets to another. Used by browser sandboxes (privileged process opens, passes fd to sandbox). Daemon supervisors (systemd's socket activation).

sub_mechanisms.name: shm_open_memfd
sub_mechanisms.definition: Modern shared memory: shm_open(name) or memfd_create(name) returns fd; mmap it for shared access.
sub_mechanisms.why: Replaces legacy SysV shm. fd-based interface integrates with select/poll/CLOEXEC/sendfile/etc. memfd_create with MFD_SEAL prevents truncation/write — useful for safely sharing.

sub_mechanisms.name: POSIX_signals_realtime
sub_mechanisms.definition: SIGRTMIN..SIGRTMAX (32-64): real-time signals queued + carry a payload (sigval). Standard signals are not queued.
sub_mechanisms.why: Standard signals coalesce: multiple identical signals before handling become one. RT signals queue + carry data → reliable async notification. Used by some servers for fd-ready notification (deprecated in favour of eventfd).

sub_mechanisms.name: eventfd
sub_mechanisms.definition: fd that holds a 64-bit counter. write adds; read returns (and clears or decrements). Wakeable via poll/epoll.
sub_mechanisms.why: Lightweight signalling. One process writes; another reads. Integrates with epoll. Replaces self-pipe trick. Used by libraries to signal events to event loops.

sub_mechanisms.name: signalfd
sub_mechanisms.definition: fd that delivers signals. read returns signalfd_siginfo per pending signal. Integrates with poll/epoll.
sub_mechanisms.why: Synchronous signal handling: no async-safe constraints. Process can read signals as data from event loop. Critical for sane signal handling in modern code; the alternative (async handlers) is a minefield.

sub_mechanisms.name: timerfd
sub_mechanisms.definition: fd that fires on timer expiration. Set timeout via timerfd_settime. Read returns expiration count. Integrates with poll/epoll.
sub_mechanisms.why: Lets timers integrate with event loop. Alternative to signal-based timers (SIGALRM). Each fd = one timer; combine many in epoll.

sub_mechanisms.name: dbus_messaging
sub_mechanisms.definition: D-Bus: high-level IPC bus on Linux. Brokered: messages go through dbus-daemon. Used by systemd, GNOME, KDE.
sub_mechanisms.why: Structured messaging with names + signatures + signals + properties. Higher-level than raw sockets. Cost: broker overhead. Modern: kdbus/bus1 attempted to move into kernel (failed); sd-bus is more efficient than dbus-daemon for systemd's use.

sub_mechanisms.name: shared_memory_with_futex
sub_mechanisms.definition: Shared memory region + futex on a shared variable inside it. Producer + consumer coordinate via futex_wait/wake.
sub_mechanisms.why: Highest-throughput IPC. Zero-copy data exchange. Futex for synchronisation. Used in: LMAX Disruptor, network packet rings (DPDK, AF_XDP), database shared buffers.

derivation_rules.name: shared_memory_zero_copy_beats_pipes
if: bulk data is exchanged frequently between processes
then: shared memory beats pipes/sockets at throughput
derivation_rules.why: Pipes: kernel buffer + 2 copies (user→kernel + kernel→user). Sockets: same. Shared memory: zero copy, direct memory access. For GB/s throughput, shared memory is the only option.

derivation_rules.name: fd_passing_safer_than_path_based_sharing
if: a process needs another to access an opened resource
then: fd passing avoids race conditions of path-based sharing
derivation_rules.why: Path can change between processes (TOCTOU). fd refers to a specific file description. Browser sandboxes use this: privileged opens, sandboxed accesses via passed fd. The file might not even be accessible by name to the receiver.

derivation_rules.name: signalfd_avoids_async_signal_minefield
if: a process handles signals via signalfd
derivation_rules.why: Async handler: only ~50 safe syscalls. signalfd handler: any code, runs in normal context. Modern code uses signalfd or self-pipe trick precisely to escape async constraints.

derivation_rules.name: eventfd_integrates_signalling_with_epoll
if: a thread needs to signal another's event loop
derivation_rules.why: Standalone signals require special handling in event loop. eventfd is just an fd — same code path as sockets, pipes. One eventfd per event source. The modern Linux pattern.

derivation_rules.name: pipe_buffer_provides_flow_control
if: a slow consumer reads from a pipe
then: the producer blocks when buffer fills
derivation_rules.why: Natural backpressure without explicit signalling. Producer can't outrun consumer. Standard shell pipeline behaviour. Failure mode (SIGPIPE on broken pipe) signals consumer death cleanly.
